Masked-Cell Validation (In-Sample, No Refit)

Source: R/profile_validate_masked.R
profile_validate_masked.Rd

Masks a reproducible, eligibility-preserving subset of genuinely observed cells in Y and predicts them from the already-fitted model (fit_result) – honestly an in-sample conditional-prediction diagnostic (validation_mode = "in_sample_no_refit"), since the masked cells still contributed to fitting beta/eta, not a genuine held-out test. Useful for a quick miscalibrated-subgroup scan; prefer profile_validate_heldout for the real holdout.

Usage

profile_validate_masked(
  fit_result,
  design,
  Y,
  ids,
  fraction_to_mask = 0.05,
  max_mask_per_cell = NULL,
  min_tested_after_mask = 10L,
  min_resistant_after_mask = 3L,
  min_susceptible_after_mask = 3L,
  n_draws = 500L,
  seed = 123L
)

Arguments

fit_result

List from profile_fit_joint_bernoulli (reads $fit).

design

List from profile_build_design (reads $stan_data: X, B, V).

Y, ids

The SAME Y matrix and ids data frame passed to profile_build_design (via profile_prepare_model_data) – the observed side of every comparison comes from these, not re-derived from raw data.

fraction_to_mask

Numeric in (0, 1]. Target fraction of observed cells to mask per group x class cell, before the eligibility floor and max_mask_per_cell cap. Default 0.05.

max_mask_per_cell

Integer or NULL. Optional additional cap.

min_tested_after_mask, min_resistant_after_mask, min_susceptible_after_mask

Integer. Panel-eligibility floors enforced during masking. Default 10L, 3L, 3L.

n_draws

Integer. Posterior draws used (subsampled if the fit has more). Default 500L.

seed

Integer. Mask selection AND posterior-draw-subsampling seed. Default 123L.

Value

Named list: predictions (one row per masked cell: group, event_row, class, true_value, predicted_resistance_probability, predicted_class, log_score, brier_score, validation_mode), summary (one-row aggregate: counts, mean log/Brier score, log_loss (the LogLoss convention, lower-is-better – the NEGATIVE of mean_log_score, both reported so the sign is never ambiguous), accuracy, auroc (NA, not 0, with one-class truth), average_precision, calibration_intercept/ calibration_slope (NA when unestimable)), and calibration (binned predicted-vs-observed calibration curve).
